summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and constipation. She had severe epigastric pain radiating to the right side, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, with no relief from her usual oral Dilaudid. Labs showed leukocytosis and mild metabolic abnormalities. Imaging confirmed appropriate GJ tube placement without obstruction. She was treated with IV fluids, pain control using scheduled IV Dilaudid, and initiation of oral naloxone for opioid-induced constipation, which led to a successful bowel movement. She advanced to clear liquids and tolerated tube feeds. A Code Purple occurred when she attempted to take unauthorized pills, leading to sedation with Ativan and Zyprexa. Antibiotics for mild G-tube site erythema were discontinued after reassessment. Her insulin regimen was continued without change. She was discharged home with an aggressive bowel regimen, clear instructions on pain management, and follow-up plans.
